# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need convey the manual’s rule to Deaf without speech. Since the table’s rows are ordered blue, red, yellow and each row maps a light color to the identical wire color, I’ll use three distinct gesture pairs in that order: each repeated pair represents the same color on both sides of a row. Deaf can then identify the illuminated color and tell Blind which matching wire to cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👌", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have found nothing actionable. Please read the manual and tell me its exact rule. Also obtain Deaf's complete report of every colour and marking on the bomb, then relay both the manual rule and Deaf's report to me next round.

The manual’s exact rule is an identity mapping: whichever light colour is present, Blind must cut the wire of that same colour. I need Deaf to relay that rule to Blind and report every visible colour and marking from the bomb; I’ll signal both the established three-row mapping and a request for the complete visual report.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👌", "👌", "🫵", "🤳", "🤲"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received Deaf's report: display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot perceive your gestures. Please speak the manual's exact rule, including which wire position to cut.

The required action is clear: the yellow light means cut the yellow wire, which is wire position 2. Blind cannot receive my gestures, so I must instruct Deaf to convey this verbally. I’ll use a pointing gesture for the light, a matching/identity gesture for “same colour,” and two fingers for wire position 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤝", "✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please now gesture exactly one symbol for the wire position required by the manual: thumbs-up means wire 1, thumbs-down means wire 2, and OK means wire 3. Deaf will report the symbol aloud to me.

The yellow light requires cutting the yellow wire, which is wire position 2. Blind has defined the required encoding, so I should send exactly one thumbs-down gesture for Deaf to report aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the manual rule aloud in plain words, including the exact wire position to cut. Gestures cannot convey it to me.

I cannot speak aloud as Mute. Deaf can see my gestures and can relay the instruction by voice to Blind. The established thumbs-down symbol means wire 2; I’ll send it again, along with the previously used “same/matching” gesture so Deaf can state that the wire colour must match the light colour.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still cannot interpret the gesture sequence. Speak the manual's rule in plain words now, including the exact wire position to cut. Do not gesture.

As Mute, I have no voice channel, so I cannot speak the rule directly to Blind. The only viable relay is Deaf: Deaf already knows the light is yellow, and I will signal the established “matching colour” instruction and wire 2, so Deaf can state plainly that wire 2, the yellow wire, must be cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The correct wire remains wire 2, because the light is yellow and the manual requires cutting the wire of the same colour. I cannot speak, so I can only remind Deaf of the agreed wire-2 signal for relay to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous bomb was defused, and the bomb has changed, but no new visual report or manual rule has arrived. I have no basis for a safe instruction yet, so I should not send an ambiguous gesture.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: For the current state, please gesture exactly one wire position required by the manual: thumbs-up means position 1, thumbs-down means position 2, and OK means position 3. Deaf, relay only that one symbol.

The current bomb’s light and wire arrangement have not been reported to me, so I cannot determine a safe wire position. Sending any of the three symbols would be an unsupported guess and could detonate the bomb. I will wait rather than transmit a potentially wrong position.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms another correct cut and a changed bomb, but no current light, markings, or wire report has been provided. I cannot safely determine the next wire position, so I will wait for the new state to be reported.

```text
wait()
```
